summary: - _(e) Pass any such further order as this Commission may deem necessary in the interest of justice.”_ 8. The matter was first heard on 14.6.2022, wherein the Respondent Discoms were directed not to take coercive action against the Petitioner and the parties were directed to complete their respective pleadings. Subsequent hearings were held on 15.9.2023, 2.7.2025, and 28.8.2025, during which time was sought to complete the pleadings. (g) In terms of Article 8.6 of the PPA, if the Procurer (Respondent Discoms), without disputing any bill/invoice raised by the seller (Petitioner), continued to pay bills/invoices, such bills became final, conclusive and binding upon the parties. The decision of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in _Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Co. Ltd. vs MERC & Ors. in Civil Appeal No. 1843 / 2021_ has been relied upon by the Petitioner, wherein it was held that bills not disputed as per the procedure prescribed under the PPA stand final and conclusive. In the present case, the conduct of the Respondent Discoms in consistently honouring the invoices/ bills and raising no objection whatsoever indicates that they were fully aware of the computation mechanism, as the escalation calculations were transparently reflected in the invoices raised. The computational issue pertains to invoices/ bills raised over several years, and the Respondent cannot seek retrospective adjustments beyond the permissible period, particularly when the invoices were subject to periodic reconciliations. The Respondent Discoms signed reconciliation statements from 2014 to 201718, without raising any objections at that time, and the reconciliation process was finalised for the period from March 2018 to March 2021. 12. Upon completion of the pleadings, the matter was heard on 27.10.2025, wherein the parties made detailed oral submissions. In response to a specific query from the Commission regarding the reference of the disputes to arbitration, the parties filed their respective written submissions on the issue of reference of the disputes to arbitration. Thereafter, on 20.11.2025, after hearing the parties on the issue of arbitrability, the Commission reserved its order on the question of ‘arbitrability’ and observed that depending upon the outcome thereof, the Petition may thereafter be listed for hearing ‘on merits’. (d) The dispute in the present case is not a simpliciter recovery claim nor a case of breach or termination of contract. It does not pertain to damages, liquidated damages, or any independent contractual claim detached from the (a) The dispute involved in the present case and the reliefs sought therein are not arbitrable and ought not to be referred to arbitration. A dispute between a generating company and a distribution licensee, in matters connected with the regulation of tariff, falls squarely within the exclusive jurisdiction of this Commission. Neither the PPA nor the parties agree to the reference of the dispute to arbitration. (d) The Petition has been filed for adjudication by this Commission over the correctness or otherwise of the invoices raised, on the basis of the provisions concerning the computation of tariff. The judgment in the _DVC vs MPPMCL_ case held that all matters which would have a bearing upon the tariff for a generating company would constitute a tariff dispute and fall solely within the jurisdiction of this Commission and are not arbitrable. (f) The decision of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in _Union of India & Ors. Vs. Uttar Pradesh State Bridge Corporation Ltd., [(2015) 2 SCC 52]_ , as relied upon by the Petitioner, held that the first and paramount principle of A&C Act is the disposal of disputes in a fair, speedy, effective, inexpensive and expeditious manner, and unnecessary delay or expense would frustrate the very purpose of arbitration. A reference to arbitration, in the present case, when the same had been before this Commission for a considerable period of time, defeats the primary object of arbitration. (g) The reliance on the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in _BALCO vs. Kaiser Aluminium Technical Services INC. [(2016) 4 SCC 126]_ , wherein it has been held that party autonomy is the brooding and guiding spirit of arbitration. The parties in the present Petition are ad idem that the dispute in the present case involves a tariff dispute, liable to be adjudicated by this Commission and not covered by the arbitration clause in the PPA. 15. We have considered the rival contentions of the parties on the issue of arbitration and observe that the parties, in their respective submissions, have unequivocally contended that the disputes raised in the present Petition pertain to the computation and application of the escalation index that forms part of the tariff structure under the PPA. Both parties are _ad idem_ that adjudication by this Commission is necessary to effectively resolve the dispute. Thus, the limited issue before us at this stage is whether the dispute raised in the Petition must be adjudicated by the Commission or referred to arbitration.
